def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    N = int(data[0])
    P = [int(x) for x in data[1:1+N]]

    # Fenwick tree of size N, each position initially has value 1 (available)
    size = N

    while (1 << LOG) <= size:
        LOG += 1
    LOG -= 1  # largest power of two <= size

    bit = [0] * (size + 1)
    # Initialize: each index 1..N has value 1
    # Efficient build:
    for i in range(1, size + 1):
        bit[i] += 1
        j = i + (i & -i)
        if j <= size:
            bit[j] += bit[i]

    def update(i, delta):
        while i <= size:
            bit[i] += delta
            i += i & -i

    def find_kth(k):
        # find smallest index i such that prefix sum >= k
        idx = 0
        r = LOG
        while r >= 0:
            nxt = idx + (1 << r)

        pos = find_kth(P[i-1])
        result[pos] = i
        update(pos, -1)

    max_idx = (1 << (LOG + 1)) - 1

    # Initialize the base available spots (1 if i <= N, 0 otherwise)
    for i in range(1, N + 1):
        bit[i] = 1
        
    # Build the Fenwick tree in O(max_idx) time
    for i in range(1, max_idx + 1):
        j = i + (i & -i)
        if j <= max_idx:
            bit[j] += bit[i]
            
    result = [0] * (N + 1)
    start_step = 1 << LOG
    
    # Process queries in reverse to find the final landing positions
    for i in range(N, 0, -1):
        k = int(input_data[i])  # k is P_i
        
        # find_kth: binary lifting on Fenwick tree avoids out-of-bounds checks
        # because the tree size is exactly (1 << (LOG + 1)) - 1
        idx = 0
